note: LB.10a identity fixture (legacy-only, no matrix cell). Every C/C++ file is its own MODULE, named by its full file name, because an #include names a file with its extension: Widget.h and Widget.cpp are src::Widget.h and src::Widget.cpp, and each #include "Widget.h" IMPORTS src::Widget.h. A .h is parsed with the C++ grammar unless the C grammar parses it with fewer errors (c/point.h names a parameter `template`, a C identifier the C++ grammar rejects; tree-sitter-cpp reads `class` / `new` / `this` as identifiers without an error), declarations inside #ifndef include guards are visited, and a bodiless class/struct specifier (a forward declaration) mints no type. HEAD: both halves are MODULE src::Widget (with a self-IMPORTS edge), the guarded class is dropped so no CLASS Widget exists, and `class Gadget;` mints a CLASS.
